items.title: Send these readings to your care team this week
items.text: Your blood sugar readings were higher than the target, so contact your care team this week. Your average reading was 172.0 mg/dL, and 5.7% of readings were above 250 mg/dL.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after meals may be linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with a walk after dinner having about an 18.3 mg/dL smaller rise. Walking 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain, with a 17.5 mg/dL smaller rise.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Having dinner at 8 pm or later, which happened 50.0% of the time, may be linked to a rise in sugar, with a 9.2 mg/dL larger rise after late dinners. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 11.9 hours, and research showed that a longer overnight fast changed HbA1c by -0.03 points. You might consider trying to extend your overnight fast, but check with your care team first.
